observe_how: Grep of repo .claude/settings.json finds ZERO occurrences of 'package-install-guard' or 'plan-mode-approval-gate' (the repo's Bash matcher group carries only navigator-safety; there is no ExitPlanMode matcher group at all), while the active ~/.claude/settings.json registers both (Bash matcher for the install guard, ExitPlanMode matcher for the gate). SEED-15 already covers the template gap for package-install-guard; the NEW evidence here is (a) plan-mode-approval-gate is in the same active-only bucket, and (b) the drift is in the checked-in .claude/settings.json itself, not just settings.json.template — so a repo-driven rebuild or new machine ships with neither the supply-chain guard nor the plan-approval gate. title: agent-model-guard validates agent existence ONLY against ~/.claude/agents — project-level .claude/agents/ and plugin-provided agents are denied as nonexistent (fail-closed against valid spawns)
observe_how: Claude Code resolves subagent types from project-level <project>/.claude/agents/ and from plugin caches in addition to ~/.claude/agents/, but the guard's lookup is hardcoded to homedir. In continuous-claude the sync script masks this (repo agents mirror to ~/.claude/agents), but any other project carrying local-only agents, or any plugin-defined agent type, gets a hard DENY for an agent the harness could actually spawn. The hardcoded BUILTIN_AGENTS set is a second fragile allowlist — a new builtin type added by a Claude Code release is denied until someone edits this file. Note also the file is misnamed: despite 'model-guard' it does existence validation only (the model guard is no-haiku-enforcer); the header was already retitled 'Agent Existence Validation Hook'. Fix: also probe CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/agents, and fail open (warn) rather than deny on unknown types.
telemetry: Search hook logs for 'not found at' deny messages naming agents that exist in a project's .claude/agents/.

title: no-haiku-enforcer (and navigator-validate) only block the exact string 'haiku' — full model ids like 'claude-haiku-4-5' pass the deny check
observe_how: The no-haiku rule is absolute ('never set model: haiku — no exceptions') but the Agent tool accepts full model ids; `model: 'claude-haiku-4-5'` (or any dated haiku id) sails through both checks. Payoff: one-line change to `.includes('haiku')` closes the gap.
telemetry: Spawn a Task with model 'claude-haiku-4-5' and observe no deny.

title: tldr-context-inject is unreachable under EITHER tool name (matcher "Agent" + internal `tool_name !== 'Task'` gate reject each other's world) and carries a latent Windows infinite loop in findProjectRoot plus fabricated 'line 10' PDG slices

evidence.quote: const targetLine = lineNumber || 10;  // Default to line 10 if no line specified

causal_links: hang amplitude set by D2b-07 (no real timeout)
observe_how: If tool is named 'Task': matcher "Agent" never fires. If tool is named 'Agent': the hook runs but L420 immediately prints '{}' because tool_name is 'Agent' not 'Task'. Net: the hook can never inject — registered dead weight executed-or-skipped on every spawn. Latent hazards if revived: path.win32.dirname('C:\\')==='C:\\' so the `while (current !== '/')` loop never terminates when no project marker exists above cwd; PDG slices are fabricated at line 10 when no line is mentioned; the catch-all extractor regex /[`"']?([a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,})[`"']?/g (L130) treats nearly any English word as a code symbol (same pollution class as SEED-13). It also emits `updatedInput` to rewrite the agent prompt — the only hook using the documented modify key, but pointless while unreachable.
telemetry: No fire evidence; uses daemon `track` channel only on the success path which is unreachable

title: file-claims (LIVE on every Edit/Write in every project) spawns 2-3 fresh `uv run python` + asyncpg processes per edit with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in the read path, and a DB error in isSessionActive silently converts an ACTIVE peer's lock into a takeover
causal_links: SEED-12 (getSessionId scheme split feeds the claim identity)
D2b-13 (project+user dual registration would double the spawns if not deduped)
observe_how: file-claims.ts main(): checkFileClaim (1 uv+python+asyncpg spawn, which re-runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS on every read, db-utils-pg.ts L613-621) + claimFile (2nd spawn) on every Edit/Write; conflict path adds isSessionActive (3rd spawn). Per SEED-08, uv-run startup is the dominant cost — call it 0.5-2s per spawn, so 1-4s tax per edit. Correctness: on ANY isSessionActive failure (DB down, 3s timeout) it returns false -> file-claims.ts L80-82 'Other session is stale - take over the claim' steals the lock from a genuinely active session — the exact conflict the hook exists to block. Latent landmine: the Python-side default URL in isSessionActive says port 5434 while checkFileClaim/claimFile say 5432 (dead today because runPgQuery always injects CONTINUOUS_CLAUDE_DB_URL, but the first refactor that drops that env hits it). Also TOCTOU: check-then-claim is non-atomic across two processes.
telemetry: SEED-08: warm uv-run latency 13-17s on recall path corroborates the startup tax; runPgQuery timeout is 3000ms per spawn (db-utils-pg.ts L71)
